Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

Fitted candidates (all on the same data, 126 readings):

Candidate C9 (asprey_2000_monod_kinetics eq 17, rate law r = theta1*x2/(theta2 + x2)):
asprey_2000_monod_kinetics + asprey_2000_monod_kinetics eq 17: chi2 2249.9 vs limit 148.8 (p = 0.000) (LACK OF FIT); AIC 2257.9; probability 0.000

   theta2   0.05805  95% CI [0.05368, 0.06242]  t 13.28
   theta3   0.5499  95% CI [0.5388, 0.561]  t 49.57
   theta4   0.08444  95% CI [0.07977, 0.08911]  t 18.09

asprey_2000_monod_kinetics + zentou_2019_andrews eq 5: chi2 103.4 vs limit 147.7 (p = 0.875) (fits within the noise); AIC 113.4; probability 1.000

Round 1 of 3. Decide. If you accept, 'chosen' is the candidate label, e.g. C9.

answer.feedback: Accept C40, the Andrews substrate-inhibition rate law. It fits within the noise (chi2 103.4, below the 95% limit of 147.7), all parameter t-values exceed 1, and it has Akaike weight 1.000. C9 and C8 show severe lack of fit, especially under-prediction of substrate in E3. Note that only 2 of 4 starting points reached this fit; checking optimization robustness would be prudent.
answer.reasoning: C40 satisfies the acceptance criteria: adequate fit and every parameter is estimated precisely. It is decisively preferred among the fitted candidates by Akaike weight. The unsuccessful starts are an optimization caveat, not evidence against the reported fit.
